faq.q: Why do you charge for an inspection when others are free?
faq.a: Because it is different work. A free estimate is a salesperson looking at your wall so they can quote you. A paid assessment is a technician with thermal imaging and moisture meters producing a document with photographs, findings and a priced scope. You own it, and you can take it to an insurer, an engineer or a competitor. If you hire us for the repair, the fee comes off the invoice.

faq.q: How much does an assessment cost?
faq.a: Partial assessments covering up to two areas start at $500. A full property assessment starts at $750. Multi-unit properties are assessed per unit. The fee is credited against the repair if you go ahead with us.

faq.q: How long does the guarantee last?
faq.a: Three years on workmanship, covering the labour on exterior repairs and installations we carry out. If something comes up under it we respond within 48 hours.

faq.q: Do you work on commercial property?
faq.a: Yes. Alongside one-off commercial work we run three ongoing plans: a Commercial Service Plan, Preventive Maintenance, and Emergency Readiness. Property managers tend to want a schedule and a named contact rather than a phone number to call in a crisis.

faq.q: How quickly can you get to an emergency?
faq.a: Same day where we can. If water is moving through the building right now, call rather than filling in a form. The difference between a drying job and a mold remediation job is often 48 hours.

faq.q: Do I need a mold test before remediation?
faq.a: Often not. If you can see it and smell it, a laboratory will only confirm what you already know. Testing earns its cost when the growth is hidden, when a health question is live, or when a transaction or dispute needs a documented result.

faq.q: Will you remediate mold without fixing the leak?
faq.a: No. It would come back and you would be entitled to be angry about it. If you cannot fund both at once we will scope the source repair first and stage the remediation.

That depends on your policy and the cause of loss, and we will not guess before seeing it. What we can do is document the loss to the standard adjusters expect, which is where homeowners most often lose money.

faq.q: What technology do you actually use?
faq.a: FLIR thermal imaging to find the temperature difference wet material creates, pin and pinless moisture meters to confirm it in real numbers, drone survey for roofs and upper elevations, and invasive probing on stucco where surface inspection tells you nothing.
We cover Philadelphia, the surrounding suburbs and northern Delaware. Florida is opening soon. Enter your ZIP anywhere on the site and we will tell you straight away.

quiz.intro: Eight questions, about sixty seconds. You get a read on how urgent it looks before anyone asks you for anything.

opts: I have noticed a specific issue
Something feels off but I am unsure
I manage a building or portfolio

questions.ask: What type of property is this?
What are you trying to accomplish?
How long has this been happening?

bands.name: Low risk
bands.head: Nothing here looks urgent.
bands.body: What you have described reads as low risk. That does not mean nothing is happening, only that there is no sign of it moving fast. A video consultation is the cheapest way to be sure before you spend anything.

bands.name: Moderate risk
bands.head: There are signs of moisture getting in.
bands.body: This pattern usually means intermittent leaks or dampness building behind a wall or ceiling. It rarely feels urgent at this stage, which is exactly why it gets expensive. An assessment will tell you where it is coming from.

bands.name: High risk
bands.head: This needs looking at soon.
bands.body: Several answers point to active, spreading water. At this stage the difference between a drying job and a full remediation is often days, not weeks. Book an assessment, or call us if water is moving right now.
